title: Korean border talks, Europe's deadly heat and a melanoma vaccine

stories.headline: South Korea invites the North to military talks over the border
stories.headlineZh: 韩国邀请朝鲜就边界问题举行军事会谈
stories.summaryZh: 九月非军事区爆炸致三名韩国士兵受伤后，首尔提议与平壤会谈以缓和边境紧张局势。
stories.c1:
South Korea has invited North Korea to formal military talks in a bid to defuse tensions that have been simmering along one of the world's most heavily fortified borders. The offer, announced by Seoul's defence ministry on Friday, 23 October, would see the two sides sit down to confirm exactly where the land Military Demarcation Line runs, restore military communication lines and work out ways of preventing accidental clashes.

The proposal comes in the wake of a series of incidents that have rattled the frontier. In September, explosions near the demarcation line in the western part of the Demilitarized Zone injured three South Korean soldiers. Seoul blamed landmines laid by the North and demanded an apology, but Pyongyang flatly rejected the accusation.

Officials in Seoul suggested that dates and venues could be arranged through Panmunjom, the truce village where soldiers from both sides stand face to face, and said they would be open to involving the US-led United Nations Command. The ministry warned that it was hard to predict what further incidents might occur if the situation were left unaddressed.

Whether the North will take up the offer is far from certain. Under Kim Jong Un, Pyongyang has suspended almost all dialogue and cooperation with the South in recent years, and a similar proposal last year went unanswered. Kim's sister, Kim Yo Jong, has said new military units have been moved into firing positions along the border, and she dismissed President Lee Jae Myung's calls for talks as "the climax of the farce". Still, by putting a concrete agenda on the table, Seoul has at least signalled that it would rather talk than escalate.
stories.b2:
South Korea has invited North Korea to official military talks to reduce tension along one of the most heavily guarded borders in the world. The defence ministry in Seoul announced the offer on Friday, 23 October. It wants both sides to agree on exactly where the land border runs, bring back military communication lines and find ways to avoid accidental fighting.

The offer follows several worrying incidents. In September, explosions near the border in the western part of the Demilitarized Zone injured three South Korean soldiers. Seoul said the North had laid landmines there and asked for an apology, but Pyongyang strongly denied this.

South Korean officials said the dates and place of the talks could be organised through Panmunjom, the village where soldiers from both countries stand face to face. They also said the US-led United Nations Command could take part. The ministry warned that more incidents could happen if nothing is done.

Nobody knows if the North will accept. In recent years it has stopped almost all contact with the South, and it did not reply to a similar offer last year. Kim Jong Un's sister, Kim Yo Jong, has said new military units are now in firing positions along the border.

vocab.example: The café cut its prices in a bid to win back regular customers.

vocab.en: make a tense situation calmer and less dangerous
vocab.example: Our manager made a joke to defuse tensions during the heated meeting.

vocab.en: strongly protected with military defences
vocab.example: The embassy is now heavily fortified after last year's protests.

vocab.en: following and often caused by an event
vocab.example: Airport security was tightened in the wake of the incident.

vocab.en: to make someone or something nervous or unsettled
vocab.example: The sudden fall in share prices rattled investors.

vocab.en: refuse completely and firmly
vocab.example: The council flatly rejected the developer's new proposal.

vocab.en: accept something that has been offered

vocab.en: very uncertain

questions.q: North Korea has admitted that it laid the landmines.
questions.explain: 文中说 Pyongyang “flatly rejected the accusation”，即断然否认，与题干矛盾。

questions.q: Explosions in the Demilitarized Zone injured three South Korean soldiers in September.
questions.explain: 原文：“In September, explosions ... injured three South Korean soldiers”，与题干一致。

questions.q: Which of the following is one aim of the proposed talks?
options: To agree on a peace treaty ending the Korean War
To arrange a meeting between the two leaders
To confirm where the land border actually runs
To remove all landmines from the Demilitarized Zone
questions.explain: 原文提到会谈要 “confirm exactly where the land Military Demarcation Line runs”，其他选项文中未提。

questions.q: The United Nations Command has already agreed to join the talks.
questions.explain: 文中只说首尔 “would be open to involving” 联合国军司令部，并未说明对方是否同意。

stories.discuss: Why do you think countries in a long-running conflict often find it so hard to start talking? Can small practical steps, like restoring a hotline, lead to bigger changes?

stories.headline: Europe's summer heat killed over 50,000 people in its cities
stories.headlineZh: 欧洲今夏高温致城市逾五万人死亡
stories.summaryZh: 新研究估计欧洲854座城市今夏有50391人死于高温，约三分之二与气候变化有关。
stories.c1:
Europe's scorching summer may have claimed more than 50,000 lives in its cities, according to a new study, and researchers believe roughly two-thirds of those deaths would not have happened without human-caused climate change. Modelling 854 cities through the heatwaves of June, July and August, the team estimated 50,391 heat-related deaths, of which 32,619 were attributed to the extra warmth from burning fossil fuels.

If the estimate holds up, this summer would be by far the deadliest in recent records, with a toll 71% higher than that of 2022, the previous worst. Italy, France, Spain and Germany bore the brunt, and more than half of those who died were aged 85 or older, although over 800 deaths were among people aged 20 to 44. Some cities sweltered at 12°C above normal.

Because heat is rarely recorded on death certificates, the figures rely on statistical modelling rather than direct counts. The researchers compared actual conditions with a simulated world without climate change, and checked their method against official UK data, which it matched closely, if not perfectly. The authors concede that the total is probably an underestimate, since it leaves out a deadly May heatwave and covers cities home to only about 40% of Europe's population.

The study, due to appear in the journal Nature Health, has prompted renewed calls for action. Outside experts urged governments to invest in early-warning systems, affordable low-carbon cooling and check-in programmes for vulnerable residents. Several stressed, however, that adapting to the heat is not enough on its own: cutting fossil fuel use must go hand in hand with it.
stories.b2:
A new study suggests that more than 50,000 people died because of heat in Europe's cities this summer. The researchers believe about two-thirds of these deaths would not have happened without climate change caused by humans. They studied 854 cities during the heatwaves of June, July and August and estimated 50,391 deaths, with 32,619 linked to extra heat from burning fossil fuels.

If the figure is correct, this summer was much deadlier than 2022, the previous worst year, with 71% more deaths. Italy, France, Spain and Germany were hit hardest. More than half of the people who died were 85 or older, but over 800 were aged between 20 and 44.

Heat is rarely written on death certificates, so the team used statistical models instead of counting deaths directly. They compared real conditions with a computer-made world without climate change. The authors say the real total is probably higher, because the study did not include a deadly heatwave in May and covered only about 40% of Europe's population.

Experts not involved in the study called for early-warning systems, cheap low-carbon cooling and programmes that check on vulnerable people. But they said that reducing fossil fuel use is also necessary.

vocab.en: cause people to die
vocab.example: The floods claimed dozens of lives across the region.

vocab.en: say that something is caused by something else
vocab.example: Doctors attributed his recovery to early treatment.

vocab.en: remain true or valid when examined

vocab.en: a figure or judgement that is too low

vocab.en: be closely connected or happen together
vocab.example: Good sleep and good health go hand in hand.

questions.q: The researchers counted heat deaths directly from death certificates.
questions.explain: 原文说 “the figures rely on statistical modelling rather than direct counts”，与题干矛盾。

questions.q: Why do the authors think the real number of deaths is probably higher?
options: The study ignored a May heatwave and many areas outside the cities studied
Many hospitals refused to share their data
The UK figures were much higher than their estimate
They only counted people aged over 85
questions.explain: 原文：“it leaves out a deadly May heatwave and covers cities home to only about 40% of Europe's population”。

questions.q: Rome recorded more heat deaths than any other city this summer.
questions.explain: 文中只提到意大利、法国、西班牙和德国死亡人数最多，没有提到罗马。

questions.q: More than half of the people who died were aged 85 or older.
questions.explain: 原文：“more than half of those who died were aged 85 or older”，与题干一致。

stories.discuss: Why do you think heatwaves get less public attention than floods or bushfires, even though they can kill more people? How should cities prepare for hotter summers?

stories.headline: AI uncovers hidden PHP flaws, forcing websites worldwide offline
stories.headlineZh: AI发现PHP隐藏漏洞，全球网站紧急下线
stories.summaryZh: AI协助发现PHP两个严重漏洞，多国政府网站为打补丁暂时下线。
stories.c1:
Websites around the world went dark this week as organisations scrambled to patch two critical security flaws in PHP, a programming language that is estimated to power around 70% of the web. Collectively dubbed PHP2Shell, the bugs could allow attackers to break into websites and potentially read sensitive data such as passwords.

What makes the episode particularly striking is how the flaws came to light. The security firm Calif and the Google-owned cybersecurity company Wiz both uncovered them in August with the help of advanced AI models, including one built by OpenAI. The weaknesses had apparently lain undetected for more than a decade, affecting PHP versions stretching back to 2012. OpenAI claimed that, to its knowledge, "frontier AI found these vulnerabilities before attackers did".

PHP's developers released fixes on 21 October, but the rollout was far from smooth. Details reportedly leaked a day before the planned disclosure, and Amazon's threat intelligence team said it had detected a hacking attempt before the flaws were made public. Erring on the side of caution, Finland temporarily shut down its government's public web services and the Dutch cyber-security agency took its own website offline, while the US National Security Agency advised organisations to patch immediately or pull vulnerable systems offline.

The incident highlights what many see as a double-edged sword. The same AI tools that helped defenders spot long-hidden bugs could, in the wrong hands, allow attackers to find them just as quickly. Some commentators argue that this may usher in an era in which software has to be fixed at unprecedented speed.
stories.b2:
Websites around the world went offline this week as organisations hurried to fix two serious security problems in PHP. This programming language is thought to run about 70% of the web. The bugs, called PHP2Shell, could let attackers break into websites and possibly read private information such as passwords.

The way the problems were found is unusual. The security company Calif and Wiz, a cybersecurity company owned by Google, both discovered them in August using advanced AI models, including one made by OpenAI. The weaknesses had been hidden for more than ten years and affect PHP versions going back to 2012.

PHP's developers released fixes on 21 October, but things did not go smoothly. Details reportedly leaked a day early, and Amazon said it had seen a hacking attempt before the flaws were announced. To be safe, Finland briefly closed its government's public websites, and the Dutch cyber-security agency took its own site offline. The US National Security Agency told organisations to update at once or disconnect systems at risk.

Many people say AI cuts both ways. Tools that help defenders find old bugs could also help criminals find them quickly. Software may now need to be fixed faster than ever before.

vocab.zh: 争先恐后地做；仓促应对

questions.explain: 原文：“the Google-owned cybersecurity company Wiz”，与题干一致。

questions.q: Hackers stole passwords from the Dutch cyber-security agency's website.
questions.explain: 文中只说该机构 “took its own website offline”，没有提到密码被盗。

questions.q: The flaws were first discovered in October.
questions.explain: 原文说漏洞是 “uncovered ... in August”，10月21日只是发布补丁，因此与题干矛盾。

questions.q: What did the US National Security Agency advise organisations to do?
options: Patch immediately or take vulnerable systems offline
questions.explain: 原文：NSA “advised organisations to patch immediately or pull vulnerable systems offline”。

stories.discuss: Do you think AI will make the internet safer or more dangerous overall? Why, and who should be responsible for keeping websites secure?

stories.headline: Australian-led trial finds personalised vaccine cuts melanoma's return
stories.headlineZh: 澳洲主导试验：个性化疫苗降低黑色素瘤复发风险
stories.summaryZh: 由澳洲学者领导的三期试验显示，个性化mRNA疫苗使黑色素瘤复发或死亡风险降低42%。
stories.c1:
A personalised cancer vaccine has sharply reduced the chance of melanoma returning after surgery, according to the results of a large international trial led by an Australian researcher. Georgina Long, of Melanoma Institute Australia, described the findings as "phenomenal", and the results have been accepted for publication in the New England Journal of Medicine.

The phase 3 trial, known as INTerpath-001, enrolled 1,137 patients whose melanoma was at high risk of coming back. After their tumours had been surgically removed, participants were randomly assigned to receive either the immunotherapy drug pembrolizumab with a placebo, or pembrolizumab combined with intismeran, an mRNA vaccine developed by Moderna and Merck. Crucially, the vaccine is tailor-made from each patient's own tumour, with the aim of helping the immune system target that particular cancer.

Adding the vaccine cut the risk of the cancer recurring or the patient dying by 42%, and Long reported no major harmful side effects. The study ran across 157 sites worldwide, including several Australian centres such as Westmead Hospital and the Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre. Long, who chaired the trial's steering committee and advised both companies, has been open about those industry ties.

Experts nonetheless caution against reading too much into the results just yet. Patients have so far been followed for only about 25 months, data on overall survival are still immature, and some participants did not respond to the vaccine. If the benefits prove durable, however, researchers hope the same approach could eventually be extended to other types of cancer.
stories.b2:
A personalised cancer vaccine has greatly lowered the chance of melanoma coming back after surgery, according to a large international trial led by an Australian researcher. Georgina Long, from Melanoma Institute Australia, called the results "phenomenal". They will be published in the New England Journal of Medicine.

The trial included 1,137 patients whose melanoma was likely to return. After surgery to remove their tumours, they were put into two groups by chance. One group received the immunotherapy drug pembrolizumab and a placebo. The other received pembrolizumab with intismeran, an mRNA vaccine made by Moderna and Merck. Each vaccine is made from the patient's own tumour.

Adding the vaccine lowered the risk of the cancer returning or the patient dying by 42%. Long said there were no major harmful side effects. The trial took place at 157 sites around the world, including several in Australia, such as Westmead Hospital and the Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre.

However, experts say it is too early to be sure. Patients have only been followed for about 25 months, and some did not respond to the vaccine. If the benefits last, researchers hope the method could be used for other cancers too.

vocab.en: make something much smaller or lower
vocab.example: The new timetable has sharply reduced waiting times.

vocab.en: very likely to suffer something bad
vocab.example: Older people are at high risk of heatstroke in summer.

vocab.en: put people into groups by chance, as in a scientific study
vocab.example: Students were randomly assigned to different project teams.

vocab.en: made specially for a particular person or purpose
vocab.example: The gym offers tailor-made fitness plans.

vocab.en: connections with companies in a particular business
vocab.example: Some readers questioned the report because of the author's industry ties.

vocab.en: warn people not to do something
vocab.example: Doctors caution against taking antibiotics for a cold.

vocab.en: believe something means more than it really does
vocab.example: Don't read too much into his short reply; he's just busy.

vocab.en: turn out to last a long time
vocab.example: If the peace deal proves durable, tourism could recover quickly.

vocab.en: make something apply to a wider group or area
vocab.example: The discount will be extended to part-time staff.

questions.q: All of the patients in the trial were treated in Australia.
questions.explain: 原文说试验在 “157 sites worldwide” 进行，澳洲只是其中几处，与题干矛盾。

questions.q: Why do experts say it is too early to draw firm conclusions?
options: The vaccine caused serious side effects
Patients have only been followed for about two years
The trial included too few patients
The results have not been accepted by any journal
questions.explain: 原文：“Patients have so far been followed for only about 25 months”，其余选项与原文不符。

questions.q: Each dose of the vaccine is made from the individual patient's tumour.
questions.explain: 原文：“the vaccine is tailor-made from each patient's own tumour”，与题干一致。

questions.q: The vaccine will be available in Australian public hospitals next year.
questions.explain: 文中没有提到疫苗何时、在哪里上市。

stories.discuss: Why do you think personalised medicine attracts so much hope and investment? Should expensive treatments like this be funded by the government for everyone who needs them?

dialogue.title: A Skin Check at the GP
dialogue.titleZh: 在全科诊所做皮肤检查
dialogue.setting: Priya visits her GP in Footscray for a skin check after noticing a mole that seems to have changed.
dialogue.settingZh: Priya发现一颗痣似乎有变化，于是去Footscray的全科诊所做皮肤检查。

lines.name: Dr Hughes
lines.en: Come on in, Priya. What can I do for you today?
lines.zh: 请进，Priya。今天有什么需要帮忙的？

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: There's a mole on my shoulder that I reckon has got a bit bigger.
lines.zh: 我肩膀上有颗痣，我觉得好像变大了一点。

lines.name: Dr Hughes
lines.en: Good on you for getting it looked at. How long have you noticed it?
lines.zh: 你来检查做得对。你注意到它多久了？

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: Maybe a couple of months? My partner pointed it out, to be honest.
lines.zh: 大概两三个月吧？说实话，是我伴侣先发现的。

lines.name: Dr Hughes
lines.en: Okay, let's have a proper look under the dermatoscope. Just slip your top off that side.
lines.zh: 好，我们用皮肤镜仔细看看。请把那边的衣服脱下来。

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: Sure. I've been putting this off for ages, so I'm a bit on edge.
lines.zh: 好的。我一直拖着没来，所以有点紧张。

lines.name: Dr Hughes
lines.en: That's completely understandable. The edges look fairly even, which is a good sign.
lines.zh: 完全可以理解。边缘看起来比较整齐，这是个好迹象。

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: Phew. So you don't think it's anything to worry about?
lines.zh: 呼。那你觉得没什么好担心的吧？

lines.name: Dr Hughes
lines.en: Probably not, but I'd rather be safe than sorry and take a small sample.
lines.zh: 可能没事，但为了保险起见，我想取一小块样本。

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: Fair enough. Will it hurt much? I'm a bit of a wimp with needles.
lines.zh: 有道理。会很疼吗？我挺怕打针的。

lines.name: Dr Hughes
lines.en: Just a quick sting from the local anaesthetic, then you won't feel a thing.
lines.zh: 局部麻醉时会刺一下，之后就没感觉了。

lines.name: Priya
lines.en: Alright, let's get it over and done with. When will I hear back?
lines.zh: 好吧，那就赶紧做完吧。什么时候能知道结果？

lines.name: Dr Hughes
lines.en: Results usually come through within a week. In the meantime, slip, slop, slap, okay?
lines.zh: 结果通常一周内出来。在此期间记得做好防晒，好吗？
